html:
The main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty in Seoul, Korea, built in 1395, three years after the dynasty was founded.

Its name means palace greatly blessed by heaven. It sits at the foot of Mount Bugak, laid out on a north to south line in the Chinese manner. Sejong the Great ruled from here in the 1400s, and scholars of his Hall of Worthies worked here on the new Korean alphabet that became Hangul.

In 1592, during the Imjin War, the palace burned and was left in ruins for over 270 years while kings lived in other palaces. The regent Heungseon Daewongun rebuilt it in the 1860s, at great cost, to restore royal prestige. In 1895 Japanese agents murdered Queen Min in its grounds. Under Japanese rule most buildings were torn down and a huge colonial government building was put in front of the throne hall. That building was demolished in 1995, and restoration is still under way.
sum: The main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty in Seoul, Korea, built in 1395, three years after the dynasty was founded.
